chapters.title: Anti-Harassment.
chapters.text:
Birla is committed to providing a work environment free from harassment, discrimination, intimidation, bullying, and any form of behavior that undermines the dignity of employees, contract workers, interns, trainees, visitors, or third-party personnel on company premises. Any verbal, non-verbal, written, visual, or physical conduct that denigrates or shows hostility toward an individual or their associates because of their race, color, gender, religion, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, or any other protected category is strictly prohibited. This includes actions that:
- Create an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment;
- Interfere unreasonably with an individual’s work performance;
- Adversely affect an individual’s employment opportunities;
- Undermine a person’s dignity, psychological safety, or professional reputation.
Harassment is prohibited in all work-related settings, including offices, factory premises, virtual platforms, work travel, client sites, company events, and digital communication channels.
- Types of Discriminatory Harassment: Harassment may take various forms, including but not limited to:
- Verbal abuse, slurs, jokes, or negative stereotyping that relate to an individual’s race, color, gender, religion, sexual orientation, age, national origin, or disability.
- Written or graphic materials that denigrate or express hostility towards individuals or groups based on the above attributes, which are circulated or displayed within Birla’s premises, such as on employees' desks, workspaces, equipment, or bulletin boards.
- Bullying, intimidation, exclusionary behavior, or misuse of authority that creates a hostile work environment.
Other conduct may also be considered discriminatory harassment if it meets the above criteria.
- Retaliation: Birla’s policy strictly prohibits retaliation against any individual who files a harassment complaint, raises a concern in good faith, participates in an investigation, or supports another individual in reporting misconduct. Any form of retaliation including demotion, threats, unfavorable assignments, isolation, or adverse performance reviews will be treated as a serious violation and may result in disciplinary action.
- Reporting Harassment: If you believe that you have experienced or witnessed harassment, including sexual harassment or any other discriminatory behaviour, you are encouraged to report the incident immediately. Complaints can be made through:
- Immediate Supervisor
- HR Department
- Grievance Redressal Committee
- Internal Complaints Committee (where applicable)
- Anonymous helpline or reporting channel
- If the harassment involves a third party, such as customers, vendors, contractors, or visitors, it must also be reported within 7 days so that appropriate corrective measures can be taken. All complaints will be treated confidentially to the extent possible, and records will be securely maintained.
- Investigation Process: Upon receiving a complaint, Birla will conduct a prompt, impartial, and thorough investigation. The process will include:
- Confidential interviews with the complainant, alleged respondent, and relevant witnesses
- Review of documentary or digital evidence
- Maintenance of investigation records
- Timely completion of the inquiry process
- Where required by law, investigations will be conducted in accordance with statutory provisions (e.g., applicable workplace harassment regulations). The company resolves issues fairly, objectively, and discreetly, ensuring privacy and procedural fairness for all parties involved
- Action and Disciplinary Measures: If the investigation concludes that harassment has occurred, Birla will take appropriate corrective and disciplinary action, which may include:
- Counseling or mandatory training
- Written warning
- Suspension
- Termination of employment or contract
- Removal from supervisory responsibilities
- Blacklisting of third-party offenders (where applicable)
- Corrective actions will also include preventive measures to avoid recurrence.
- Employees who report harassment or cooperate in an investigation will not face retaliation. The company will inform the complainant of the outcome of the investigation in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
## Preventive Measures for Harassment:
- Birla has institutionalized workplace conduct training programs that emphasize recognizing and addressing all forms of harassment.
- Anonymous feedback mechanisms are available to empower employees to report inappropriate behavior without fear of identification.
- Regular awareness campaigns, including posters, videos, and emails, remind employees of acceptable workplace behavior and reporting procedures.
- Monthly pulse surveys conducted by the HR department help detect early signs of discomfort or harassment within teams.
- Conflict resolution workshops are held bi-annually, equipping employees with skills to manage interpersonal disputes respectfully.

## Offer Letters and Contracts.
At Birla, we ensure clarity and transparency in all employment agreements through the issuance of formal offer letters and contracts, which outline the key terms and conditions of employment.
- Offer Letters: Upon selection for a position, an offer letter will be provided to the candidate. This letter will clearly state the terms of employment, including:
- Job title and role description
- Reporting structure
- Start date and work location
- Salary details, including pay scale and benefits
- Probation period (if applicable)
- Any other special terms and conditions
The offer letter serves as a formal document confirming the candidate's acceptance of the job offer and their understanding of the terms of employment. The candidate must sign and return the offer letter to confirm their acceptance.
- Employment Contracts: Upon acceptance of the offer, a detailed employment contract will be provided to the employee. The contract will cover:
- Duration of employment (if applicable, for fixed-term contracts)
- Salary and benefits package, including bonuses and incentives
- Working hours and attendance expectations
- Confidentiality and non-disclosure clauses (where relevant)
- Termination and resignation procedures
- Intellectual property rights (if applicable)
- Non-compete or non-solicitation agreements (if applicable)
- Any other legal obligations, including compliance with company policies
The employment contract serves as a binding agreement between Birla and the employee, ensuring mutual understanding of the terms and conditions.
## Fair Recruitment for all Individuals
At Birla, we are committed to fostering a workplace that celebrates diversity and ensures equal opportunities for all. Our recruitment practices are designed to eliminate bias and uphold inclusivity, ensuring candidates of all ages, gender identities, abilities, ethnicities, religions, differently-abled persons, and other personal attributes are treated equitably and with respect.
- Inclusive Job Advertisements and Outreach: Birla ensures that our job advertisements reflect our dedication to diversity and inclusion. We actively collaborate with advocacy groups, community organizations, and specialized job platforms to reach underrepresented groups, including minority gender identities, older professionals, and individuals with disabilities. All job postings clearly articulate our commitment to equal opportunity and non-discrimination.
- Reasonable Accommodations: Birla recognizes the unique needs of candidates and ensures reasonable accommodations are provided to support equitable access to our recruitment process. This includes accessible application formats, virtual or in-person interview options, interpreter services, and other adjustments tailored to the needs of differently-abled individuals or those requiring additional support. All requests are managed confidentially and with sensitivity.
- Equitable Selection Process: Our recruitment and selection process is designed to be free from any form of bias. Birla uses structured interviews and standardized evaluation criteria to ensure that all candidates, regardless of age, gender identity, ethnicity, or other characteristics, are assessed purely on their qualifications, experience, and potential. We train interviewers to recognize and mitigate unconscious bias, fostering a fair and inclusive evaluation environment.
- Proactive Gender and Age Diversity Measures: Birla actively works to ensure representation from minority gender identities and all age groups within our workforce. This includes tailored outreach to women in leadership, non-binary individuals, and older professionals, as well as mentorship programs aimed at nurturing diverse talent across all career stages.
- Onboarding and Integration: Every new hire at Birla is welcomed with an inclusive and personalized onboarding experience. For individuals from diverse backgrounds, we provide support such as access to affinity groups, cultural awareness training, and tailored resources to ensure a smooth integration. Employees are encouraged to share feedback on their onboarding experience to continually improve inclusivity.

chapters.title: Working Hours and Attendance.
chapters.text:
At Birla, we are committed to maintaining a balance between work and personal life while ensuring business operations run smoothly. The standard working hours and attendance procedures are outlined below.
[table]
| Work Week | Days | Work Hours |
| Standard Week | Monday to Friday | 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM |
| Lunch Break | Monday to Friday | 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM |
| Weekend | Saturday & Sunday | Off (unless otherwise specified) |
- Employees are expected to adhere to the standard working hours, unless otherwise agreed upon with their supervisor.
- Overtime may be required on occasion and will be compensated as per company policy.
At Birla, maintaining a consistent and reliable attendance record is essential for smooth operations and team collaboration. This policy outlines the procedures and expectations for employee attendance and punctuality.
## Attendance Tracking System
Birla uses Clockify for tracking employee attendance. Employees are required to log in and out of the system at the start and end of each workday. This ensures accurate recording of working hours and supports payroll processing.
## Attendance Expectations:
- Work Hours: Employees must be present during the designated working hours as per their department schedule, typically from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday to Friday, with a lunch break from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM.
- Punctuality: Employees are expected to clock in no later than the designated start time. If an employee arrives late, it must be logged in Clockify with an explanation for the delay.
- Absences: Employees must notify their supervisor in advance if they will be absent. In the case of an unplanned absence (e.g., sickness), the employee should inform their supervisor as early as possible, ideally before the start of the workday.
- Leave Requests: All leave requests (Annual Leave, Sick Leave, etc.) should be submitted through the leave management system in advance and approved by the immediate supervisor. Employees are expected to ensure proper documentation for absences exceeding 3 days (e.g., medical certificate for sick leave).
## Clock-in/Clock-out Procedure:
- Daily Attendance: Employees must use Clockify to log in and out at the start and end of each workday.
- Breaks: Time spent on breaks, including lunch, should be appropriately logged and deducted from total working hours.
- Late Arrival or Early Departure: If an employee arrives late or leaves early, it must be recorded in Clockify with the reason for the deviation. Repeated instances may lead to disciplinary action.
## Absence Reporting:
- Sick Leave: If employees are unable to attend work due to illness, they must inform their supervisor as early as possible and submit a medical certificate if absent for more than 3 consecutive days.
- Personal Leave: Employees requesting personal leave should submit a leave request through the company’s leave management system for approval at least 1-2 days in advance.
- Unscheduled Absences: In the event of unscheduled absences, employees must notify their supervisor as soon as possible. Failure to notify in a timely manner may be considered as unauthorized absence.
## Attendance Monitoring:
- Overtime: Overtime should be pre-approved by the department head. Overtime worked will be tracked through Clockify and compensated in accordance with the company’s policies.
- Absenteeism: Repeated absenteeism or tardiness, without valid reasons, will be subject to review and may result in disciplinary action as per Birla’s HR policies.
- Attendance Reports: Employees can access their attendance records through Clockify to ensure that all entries are accurate and up-to-date.
## Absence Without Notification
- If an employee is late and fails to notify their supervisor or manager in advance, or if they fail to log their time correctly in Clockify, it may be treated as an unapproved absence or unauthorized tardiness. Such instances can lead to disciplinary action.
## Employee Age Verification and Documentation.
At Birla, employees are required to provide valid documentation for employment verification and record-keeping purposes. The following documents are required:
- Identity Verification:
- Government-issued ID (e.g., Passport, Aadhar Card, Driver’s License)
- Proof of Address (e.g., Utility Bill, Bank Statement, Rent Agreement)
- Background Check:
- Educational Certificates (e.g., Degree Certificates, Transcripts)
- Previous Employment Records (e.g., Offer Letter, Experience Certificate from previous employers)
- Criminal Background Check (as per company policy)
- Age Verification:
- Educational Records: High school diploma or school-leaving certificate.
- Government-Issued ID: Birth certificate, driver’s license, or passport.
- Medical Verification: A certificate from a licensed healthcare provider (may be required at the company’s expense).
- Affidavit: In cases where official documentation is unavailable, a sworn affidavit from a parent or guardian may be submitted.

chapters.title: Promotion
chapters.text:
Promotions at Birla are based on merit, performance, competency, and the evolving needs of the business. Employees who demonstrate consistent performance, align with the company’s core values, and show potential for increased responsibility may be considered for promotion. The promotion process is structured, transparent, and free from discrimination or bias, ensuring fairness regardless of gender, age, race, religion, disability, or any other personal characteristic.
To prevent discrimination and ensure equal opportunity in career advancement, the promotion process includes the following stages:
- Performance Review: Employees are evaluated through standardized annual performance appraisals based on clearly defined objectives, measurable outcomes, behavioral competencies, and overall contribution to the organization.
- Defined Eligibility Criteria: Clear qualification, experience, and competency requirements are established for higher roles to ensure objective and consistent evaluation.
- Skill Development: Employees may be required to participate in relevant training or skill development programs to prepare for higher responsibilities. Access to such programs is communicated transparently to all eligible employees.
- Position Availability: Promotions are contingent upon the availability of higher positions within the company and organizational requirements.
- Multi-Level Review and Approval: Promotion recommendations are reviewed by the department head, HR, and senior management to ensure alignment with merit-based principles and equal opportunity standards.
- Bias Mitigation and Oversight: HR periodically reviews promotion decisions to identify and address any unintended disparities and to ensure compliance with non-discrimination policies.
- Approval Process: The final decision is made by the department head, HR, and senior management.
Promoted employees will receive formal notification with a revised job description, new compensation package, and updated benefits, where applicable.
## Transfers
Birla supports internal mobility and encourages employees to explore different roles within the organization. Transfers may be initiated based on business needs, employee development goals, succession planning requirements, or personal requests. Employees wishing to transfer to another department or location must submit a formal request to HR, which will be evaluated based on the availability of suitable roles, skills, past performance, and organizational requirements.
The transfer process involves the following:
- Transfer Request: Employees must submit a formal transfer request detailing the reason for the move, desired position, and career objectives. HR may conduct a discussion with the employee to assess readiness and skill alignment.
- Eligibility Criteria: Employees must meet defined eligibility criteria, including minimum tenure (where applicable), satisfactory performance ratings, and completion of required training programs.
- Approval Process: The transfer request will be reviewed by HR and the concerned department heads to ensure alignment with both the employee’s career growth and the company’s strategic and operational needs. All decisions will be documented to ensure transparency and consistency.
- Fair and Non-Discriminatory Review: Transfer decisions are made objectively, without discrimination based on gender, age, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic. Selection is based solely on merit, competency, and business requirements.
- Transition Plan: Upon approval, a structured transition plan will be developed, including knowledge transfer, handover timelines, reporting structure clarification, and adjustments to compensation or benefits (if applicable). Employees will be informed of all specific details in writing before the transfer is finalized.
Employees who are transferred to a new role or location will be given adequate support to ensure a smooth transition, including role-specific training, orientation programs, mentoring support (where required), and any necessary adjustments to working conditions.
Internal vacancies, wherever feasible, will be communicated through internal job postings prior to external hiring to promote equal access to opportunities.
In addition to transfers, Birla fosters internal career mobility in three key ways:
## ertical, Horizontal, and Transversal Mobility:
- Vertical Mobility: Through structured promotion pathways, employees are given the opportunity to advance to higher-level roles. Performance reviews, competency assessments, and development discussions help identify potential candidates for promotion. Succession planning frameworks are used to prepare high-potential employees for leadership roles.

chapters.title: Wage Equality
chapters.text:
At Birla, we are committed to ensuring wage equality by providing equal pay for equal work, regardless of gender, race, disability, or any other protected characteristic. Our transparent compensation structure is based on merit, skills, and performance, and we regularly review pay practices to eliminate any disparities. All employees have equal access to career development opportunities, and any concerns related to wage equality are addressed promptly and confidentially. Birla strives to foster an inclusive workplace where employees are valued and fairly compensated for their contributions.
This policy is communicated to all employees through:
- Employee induction sessions
- Display on the factory notice board
- Inclusion in the employee handbook
- Periodic worker–management meetings
All wage revisions and pay structures are approved by management and documented. Employees acknowledge their wage details through signed appointment letters and wage revision letters, which are maintained in personnel records for verification.
- Role-Based Pay Structure: Salary bands are defined based on job roles, grade levels, skills, qualifications, and responsibilities not personal characteristics. Employees performing the same role with similar experience and performance are placed within the same salary band.
- Standardized Job Evaluation: Positions are evaluated using objective criteria such as skill requirement, effort, responsibility, and working conditions to ensure consistency in pay determination.
- Documented Salary Approval Process: All salary offers, increments, and revisions are reviewed and approved by HR and Management to ensure compliance with equal pay principles.
- Monitoring of Promotions and Increments: Promotion decisions and annual increments are reviewed to ensure there is no discrimination in advancement or pay progression.
- Annual Wage Gap Reporting: We conduct an annual wage gap report in compliance with legal requirements to analyze and address pay disparities. Findings are reviewed by management and corrective actions are documented.
- Transparent Pay Practices: Our compensation structure is designed to be transparent, based on merit, skills, and performance, ensuring fairness for all employees. Salary structures are explained at the time of joining.
- Regular Pay Audits: We perform periodic internal pay equity audits comparing wages across gender, job category, and grade levels. Any identified discrepancies are reviewed by senior management, and corrective adjustments are implemented and documented where required.
- Inclusive Career Development: We ensure equal access to career growth opportunities for all employees, fostering a supportive and inclusive environment.
- Confidential Grievance Mechanism: Wage-related grievances are tracked in a grievance register and reviewed quarterly to identify any systemic concerns related to pay equity.
Birla does not permit wage discrimination under any circumstances. Any manager found responsible for unequal pay practices may be subject to disciplinary action.
At MP Birla Jute, we ensure that our employees are compensated fairly and in compliance with all statutory obligations. Our salary structure is designed to be transparent, competitive, and equitable.
The detailed salary structure is communicated to employees through:
- Appointment letters issued at the time of joining
- Individual salary break-up sheets
- Monthly payslips showing earnings and deductions
- HR explanation sessions during onboarding
All employees sign an acknowledgment of their salary structure. Payroll records are maintained and reviewed monthly by the HR and Accounts departments to ensure correct implementation
## Basic Salary
- The basic salary is the fixed component of an employee’s compensation. It forms the foundation of the salary structure and is used for calculating other allowances and benefits.
- Typically, basic salary constitutes around 40% to 50% of the total compensation.
- It is the key element for calculation of Provident Fund (PF), Gratuity, and other statutory benefits.
## House Rent Allowance (HRA)
- House Rent Allowance is provided to employees to help cover accommodation expenses. It is generally given when an employee is staying in rented accommodation.
- Typically, 40% of the basic salary for employees living in metro cities and 20% for those living in non-metro cities.
- HRA is partially taxable, and exemptions may apply based on the employee’s rent payments and city of residence.
## Special Allowance
- Special allowance is a flexible component, usually paid to employees in addition to the fixed salary. It can be adjusted based on the employee’s role, seniority, and performance.
- This is often adjusted to make the overall salary tax-efficient.
It can cover any other allowances not included under basic pay or HRA.

chapters.title: Gratuity
chapters.text:
- Gratuity is a lump sum amount paid to employees when they leave the company after completing at least 5 years of service. It is calculated based on the employee's salary and years of service.
Gratuity=(Last Drawn Salary×15×Years of Service)÷26
- Explanation:
- Last Drawn Salary: This includes basic salary and dearness allowance (if applicable).
- 15 Days’ Salary: Represents half a month's salary for every completed year of service.
- Years of Service: The total number of completed years the employee has worked. Partial years are typically rounded down to the nearest whole year.
- Divisor (26): Represents the average number of working days in a month (considering weekends).
- Gratuity is exempt from tax up to ₹20 lakhs under Section 10(10) of the Income Tax Act, depending on the length of service and the applicable rules.
## Overtime & Compensatory off Pay
- Employees are entitled to overtime pay for hours worked beyond their regular schedule, as per company policy and legal regulations. Overtime is compensated at 1.5 times the hourly basic wage rate.
- For work completed on scheduled holidays, weekly off days or during extra atypical working hours, employees who opt for additional pay instead of compensatory off days will be compensated at double their hourly basic wage rate as per company policy and legal standards.
- Compensatory off days must be utilized within 30 days of accrual, subject to manager approval and business needs.
## Other Allowances
- These allowances are paid based on the nature of the job and role. They can include:
- Telephone/Internet Allowance (for work-related calls, internet usage).
- Food and Beverage Allowance (for employees working in offices with canteens or company kitchens).
- Special Role Allowance (for employees working in critical roles like sales or operations).
- These can vary based on company policies, the nature of the role, and other factors.
## EPF and ESI Deductions.
MP Birla Jute ensures compliance with statutory regulations regarding EPF and ESI for the financial well-being of employees.
- EPF and ESI contributions are clearly reflected in monthly payslips.
- Employees are informed of their UAN number and ESI registration details at the time of enrollment.
- Contributions are deposited within statutory timelines, and challans/returns are maintained for audit verification.
- Employees are guided on how to access EPFO and ESI portals for viewing contribution status.
- Awareness sessions are conducted periodically to ensure employees understand their statutory benefits.
- EPF Accumulation: The contributions are accumulated in the employee's EPF account, which can be withdrawn under specific conditions such as retirement, resignation, or when the employee reaches the age of 58.
- ESI coverage: Provides medical benefits, disability benefits, and dependent's pension in case of work-related injuries. Coverage also extends to maternity benefits for female employees.
[table]
| Scheme | Eligibility | Contribution | Details |
| EPF | All employees with a salary less than ₹15,000 per month | Employee: 12% of basic salary, Employer: 12% of basic salary | EPF contributions are accumulated in the employee's individual EPF account and c |
| ESI | Employees earning ₹21,000 or less per month | Employee: 0.75%, Employer: 3.25% | Provides medical care, disability benefits, and dependents' pension in case of w |
Online Access: Employees can access their EPF and ESI details through the EPFO and ESI portals.

At Birla, employees are required to submit leave requests through the company's leave forms, preferably in advance. Leave requests are reviewed by supervisors and approved based on departmental requirements, with employees promptly informed of the decision. HR maintains accurate records of all leave, which employees can access for review. In case of emergencies, employees must notify their supervisor immediately and submit a formal leave request upon their return. Any abuse or misrepresentation of leave entitlements will result in disciplinary action as per company policy, ensuring effective leave management and business continuity.

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangement Policy
chapters.text:
Birla is dedicated to fostering a flexible work environment that promotes employee well-being, work-life balance, and overall productivity. The company acknowledges that flexibility can enhance employee satisfaction and performance while aligning with business needs.
## General Guidelines:
- Request Process: Employees must submit requests for flexible work arrangements at least one month in advance to the immediate supervisor and HR department via mail – hr@mpbirla.com This allows for proper evaluation and planning to ensure that operational needs are met. The request should include:
- Specific details of the flexible work arrangement (e.g., remote work, adjusted hours, compressed workweek).
- Duration of the requested arrangement (e.g., temporary or ongoing).
- Justification for the request, outlining how the employee plans to maintain productivity and meet job responsibilities while working under flexible terms.
Once submitted, the request will be reviewed based on its alignment with business goals, operational demands, and the employee's role within the team. Employees will be notified of the approval or need for adjustments within a reasonable timeframe.
- Eligibility: Flexible work arrangements may be granted depending on the nature of the role and department needs. Some roles that require on-site presence or adherence to strict schedules may have limited flexibility options.
- Performance Expectations: Employees requesting flexible work arrangements should demonstrate consistent performance and accountability. Maintaining productivity and meeting job responsibilities is essential for the approval of such arrangements.
- Approval Process: All requests must be approved by the employee’s immediate supervisor and the HR department. The impact on team collaboration, workflow, and business operations will be carefully considered before approval.
- Regular Reviews: Flexible work arrangements will be regularly reviewed to assess their effectiveness, ensuring they remain beneficial for both the employee and the company. Adjustments may be made based on business requirements or performance.
- Policy Compliance: Employees working remotely or with flexible arrangements must continue to adhere to all company policies, including those related to confidentiality, data security, and other relevant guidelines, to maintain the integrity of the company’s operations

chapters.title: Controlled use of forces and employee movement
chapters.text:
Birla is committed to maintaining a workplace environment that is both secure and respectful of employees' fundamental rights, including the right to freedom of movement and protection from intimidation, harassment, or excessive force. In balancing robust security protocols with individual liberties, we have implemented the following measures:
## Comprehensive Security Guidelines
- Security personnel are trained to follow clearly defined protocols that prioritize the dignity, rights, and safety of all employees.
- Training programs include conflict resolution, de-escalation strategies, human rights awareness, and non-violent crisis management techniques, in alignment with national laws and recognized international standards.
- Security staff are strictly prohibited from engaging in any form of harassment, intimidation, corporal punishment, coercion, or abuse of authority.
- Background verification of security personnel is conducted prior to deployment
- Security guidelines are periodically reviewed and updated to ensure compliance with evolving standards and legal requirements
- All security personnel are required to sign a Code of Conduct acknowledging acceptable behavior and disciplinary consequences for violations
- Security teams are instructed to prioritize non-violent approaches and use physical intervention only when absolutely necessary to protect employee safety or company assets from immediate threats.
- Any use of force is thoroughly documented and subject to review by management to ensure transparency, accountability, and compliance with legal and ethical standards.
- Excessive restraint, including unnecessary or prolonged use of force, physical punishment, or confinement, is strictly prohibited.
- Under no circumstances shall security personnel restrict freedom of movement by confiscating personal belongings, withholding identity documents, or locking employees inside work areas except during legally required emergency lockdowns
- Any use of force is immediately reported, thoroughly documented in an incident register, and subject to review by management and HR to ensure transparency, accountability, and compliance with legal and ethical standards
- Proven misuse of force will result in disciplinary action, including termination of service and, where applicable, reporting to legal authorities
## Monitoring and Reporting Mechanisms
- Employees have the right to confidentially report concerns related to security practices through grievance mechanisms, suggestion boxes, or direct access to HR, with a firm assurance of no retaliation.
- Awareness of this right is communicated during induction and displayed on workplace notice boards.
- All complaints are promptly investigated by the HR and Compliance teams, and corrective actions are taken when necessary to address any identified issues.
- Investigation findings and corrective measures are documented and reviewed by senior management.
- Periodic audits and reviews of security practices are conducted to ensure ongoing compliance and prevent recurrence of inappropriate behavior.
- Employees are free to enter and exit the workplace premises during scheduled working hours and breaks, subject only to reasonable security and attendance procedures.
- Security personnel are not permitted to impose arbitrary restrictions on employee movement or detain employees without justified cause.
- Any search of personal belongings must be conducted respectfully, in the presence of the employee, and without discrimination.
- Employees’ personal documents (such as identity cards, passports, or certificates) shall never be retained by security personnel or management.
- In the event of emergencies or temporary safety measures requiring movement restrictions, clear and transparent communication will be provided to ensure employees understand the reasons for the measures and cooperate accordingly.
- All temporary restrictions are time-bound, documented, and reviewed by management to ensure they are necessary and proportionate.

chapters.title: Health and Safety Guidelines.
chapters.text:
At Birla, the health, safety, and well-being of our employees are our top priority. We are committed to maintaining a safe work environment and ensuring that all employees are aware of the guidelines and procedures to prevent accidents and injuries.
## General Health and Safety Practices:
- Workplace Safety: Employees are expected to follow all safety protocols and guidelines for their specific work areas. This includes wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), following safe work procedures, and adhering to safety signs and instructions.
- Accident Reporting: In the event of an accident or injury, no matter how minor, employees must immediately report it to their supervisor or HR. An accident report will be completed, and appropriate actions will be taken.
- First Aid: Basic first aid kits are available in designated areas of the workplace. Employees trained in first aid should assist when needed, and all employees should be aware of the location of first aid resources.
- Ergonomics: Employees working at desks should maintain proper ergonomics to avoid strain and injury. Birla provides ergonomic chairs and workstations where applicable, and employees are encouraged to take regular breaks to avoid prolonged sitting.
- Health and Wellness Programs: Birla promotes a healthy work-life balance through wellness initiatives, including mental health support, fitness programs, and stress management resources.

chapters.title: Environmental Responsibility.
chapters.text:
## General Environmental Practices:
- Resource Conservation: Employees should aim to reduce waste, conserve energy, and use resources efficiently. This includes turning off lights and equipment when not in use, recycling paper, and minimizing printing.
- Waste Management: Employees are encouraged to segregate waste into the appropriate bins for recycling and disposal. We promote the reuse of materials and sustainable practices in the workplace.
- Sustainable Travel: Birla encourages employees to use public transportation, carpooling, or other sustainable travel options when commuting to work. For remote working employees, reducing unnecessary travel contributes to a lower carbon footprint.
- Eco-friendly Products: Birla seeks to use environmentally friendly products and materials in the workplace. Employees are encouraged to choose products with minimal environmental impact and reduce single-use plastic items.
- Green Initiatives: Birla fosters an environmentally responsible culture by supporting green initiatives such as tree planting, energy-efficient practices, and waste reduction campaigns.

chapters.title: Grievance Redressal
chapters.text:
The below grievance procedure provides a structured approach for employees to report complaints, ensuring timely and effective resolution.
## Types of Complaints
Employees may raise complaints on various issues, including but not limited to:
- Child labor or forced labor concerns.
- Harassment, discrimination, or diversity-related issues.
- Breaches of workplace ethics or Code of Conduct.
- Occupational health and safety incidents, risks, and concerns
- Working condition concerns.
- Human trafficking or violations of human rights.
- Workplace discrimination, violence or bullying.
- Workplace Harassment
- Retaliation related issues
- Maternity benefit-related grievances.
- Disputes regarding performance appraisals or salary reviews.
- Grievances related to termination or dismissal.
- Fraud, money laundering, or unethical practices.
- Disruptions affecting affinity or minority groups.
## Submission of Grievance
- Employees must submit a written grievance within two days of the incident, providing their name, designation, employee number, and details of the complaint.
- Submit grievances via:
- Email: complain@mpbirlajute.com
## Acknowledgment and Initial Review
- The Grievance Supervisor acknowledges the grievance, ideally on the same day.
- Grievances will be reviewed and resolved within two working days.
- Policy-level concerns are referred to the HR Head for resolution.
## Escalation to Grievance Officer
- If unresolved, the employee may escalate the grievance to the Grievance Officer, who will counsel the employee and provide a written acknowledgment.
- The Grievance Officer resolves grievances within three working days.
## Grievance Redressal Committee
- For unresolved issues, the grievance is forwarded to the Grievance Redressal Committee, comprising:
- One Functional Director.
- One HR Department representative.
- The Company Secretary.
- The committee meets within seven working days, analyzes the grievance, and submits recommendations to the Chairman.
- The Chairman’s decision is final and binding.
- The following generalized remediation procedure is followed for the above given grievances. However, the remediation procedure may be subject to changes depending upon the type of grievance. In cases involving serious human rights violations such as child labor, forced labor, bonded labor, or human trafficking, Discrimination, Harassment, Working Condition, additional protective and rehabilitative measures are implemented in line with legal and ethical requirements.
## mmediate Action
- For Safety-Related Incidents: The affected employee's safety is ensured by removing immediate risks, securing the workplace, or reassigning duties.
- For Ethical or Policy Violations: The individual involved is temporarily suspended or his/her access is restricted while the matter is under investigation.
- For Operational Concerns: Any processes or activities causing harm or non-compliance is haulted
## For Cases of Child Labor, Forced Labor, or Human Trafficking (if identified):
- The individual is immediately removed from the harmful or non-compliant situation.
- In case of underage workers, the child is withdrawn from work in a safe and responsible manner, ensuring no further harm.
- Any restriction on movement, withholding of wages, or retention of personal documents is immediately corrected.
- Senior management is informed immediately, and statutory authorities are notified where legally required.
- Protection from Retaliation: Strict measures are taken to ensure that affected individuals or whistleblowers are protected from retaliation, intimidation, or discrimination.
- For Cases of Discrimination or Harassment: The affected employee may be temporarily separated from the alleged respondent through reassignment, shift changes, or remote work arrangements (where feasible) to ensure a safe and comfortable work environment during the investigation process.
## Thorough Investigation
- Designated team or committee is assigned to investigate the grievance in a fair and unbiased manner.
- Evidence is gatheres, interviews are conducted, and relevant documents are reviewed to establish the facts.
- In cases involving labor rights violations, age verification records, recruitment documents, wage records, and contractor agreements are additionally reviewed.
- Where third-party contractors or recruitment agencies are involved, their compliance status is assessed and corrective measures are initiated if required.
- In cases of discrimination or harassment, the investigation is conducted with sensitivity, ensuring gender-appropriate representation in the committee where required, and in compliance with applicable workplace harassment laws.
- Both the complainant and respondent are provided an opportunity to present their statements and supporting evidence in a fair and impartial manner.
## Communication and Transparency
- The affected employee is kept informed about the progress of the investigation.

chapters.title: Performance Management
chapters.text:
At Birla, the performance appraisal process is designed to foster employee growth, recognize achievements, and align individual contributions with the company's goals. The process is conducted annually and involves several key steps:
- Objective Setting: At the beginning of each performance cycle, employees, in collaboration with their managers, set clear, measurable goals aligned with departmental and organizational objectives. Objectives may also include developmental goals that prepare employees for cross-functional roles or higher responsibilities, thereby supporting internal mobility. These objectives are reviewed periodically to track progress.
- Mid-Year Review: A mid-year review provides an opportunity for employees and their managers to assess progress towards goals. Adjustments to objectives, if necessary, are made during this review. This discussion also includes career aspirations, readiness for expanded roles, and potential lateral or vertical movement opportunities within the organization.
- End-of-Year Review: At the end of the year, employees and managers conduct a comprehensive performance evaluation based on agreed-upon objectives and key performance indicators (KPIs). This includes an assessment of competencies, achievements, challenges, and overall contribution to team and company goals. Performance outcomes are considered when identifying employees for internal transfers, promotions, or cross-functional assignments.
- Self-Assessment: Employees are encouraged to conduct a self-assessment, reflecting on their strengths, accomplishments, areas for improvement, and career goals. Employees are specifically encouraged to indicate interest in internal mobility, new business units, or expanded responsibilities.
- Feedback and Goal Setting for the Next Year: After the evaluation, feedback is shared in a formal one-on-one meeting. Constructive feedback focuses on strengths and areas of development. Based on this discussion, new goals are set, including development milestones that prepare employees for internal advancement or skill diversification.
- Rating and Documentation: Performance is rated on a defined scale (e.g., exceeds expectations, meets expectations, or needs improvement), and the final appraisal document is signed by both the employee and manager. This document is maintained in the employee's HR file and may be referenced for promotion decisions, internal job applications, and succession planning initiatives.
Birla believes in creating an environment of continuous feedback, where communication between employees and supervisors is open, honest, and constructive. Feedback plays a key role in employee development and internal career progression.
- Regular Check-Ins: Supervisors and managers are encouraged to have frequent check-ins with employees to discuss progress, challenges, skill development, and career aspirations. These discussions help identify employees ready for cross-functional exposure or higher responsibilities.
- 360-Degree Feedback: Birla may implement a 360-degree feedback system where employees receive feedback from peers, subordinates, and supervisors. This holistic feedback supports identification of leadership potential and readiness for internal mobility.
- Annual Feedback Survey: An annual employee survey gathers feedback on job satisfaction, management, work-life balance, and career development opportunities. Survey results are reviewed by senior management to identify improvements in internal mobility frameworks, training accessibility, and transparent promotion processes.
- Open Internal Career Dialogues: HR facilitates career discussions and internal mobility counseling sessions, enabling employees to understand eligibility criteria, skill gaps, and pathways for transitioning into new roles within the organization
## Career Development Opportunities.
Birla is committed to fostering a culture of growth and advancement, ensuring that employees have access to meaningful career development and promotion opportunities based on merit, performance, competencies, and organizational needs.
- Career Development Plans: Each employee works with their manager to create a personalized career development plan outlining short- and long-term goals, required skills, and potential growth paths. Plans may include cross-departmental exposure, project-based assignments, and structured development timelines to support internal mobility.
- Internal Job Postings: Birla values internal talent and prioritizes filling vacancies internally wherever feasible. Open positions are shared transparently through internal communication platforms, allowing eligible employees to apply before external recruitment is initiated.

Birla’s Orientation Program helps new employees seamlessly integrate into the company by providing them with essential knowledge about our culture, values, policies, and job-specific expectations.

- Workplace Familiarization: New employees are shown around the office, familiarized with safety protocols, and provided with necessary resources.

Birla’s Skill Development Programs are designed to enhance both technical and non-technical skills, supporting continuous professional growth.

- Continuous Learning Culture: Birla encourages employees to actively seek new knowledge, ensuring that training programs stay aligned with both company and personal growth needs.

At Birla, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and empowering workplace by providing women with the resources, training, and opportunities needed to thrive both professionally and personally
- Leadership Development for Women: Tailored programs to enhance leadership skills, preparing women for senior leadership roles by focusing on strategic thinking, decision-making, and team management.
- Mentorship Program: Women employees are paired with senior leaders who provide career guidance, support, and advice on overcoming challenges and advancing professionally.

chapters.title: Employee Conduct and Discipline
chapters.text:
## Types of Misconduct.
Misconduct is classified into Minor Misconduct and Major Misconduct. Actions or omissions listed below will lead to varying degrees of disciplinary action depending on the severity of the offense.
a) Minor Misconduct: Minor misconduct may result in a warning or suspension for a period of up to four days. Examples include:
- Failure to follow safety guidelines (without causing significant harm).
- Disruptive behavior on company premises.
- Negligence or careless work.
- Insubordination or failure to follow instructions.
- Unexplained absence or unauthorized leave.
- Use of company property without permission.
- Failure to maintain cleanliness and orderliness in the workspace.
- Repeated lateness or habitual tardiness.
- Improper use of company tools or equipment.
- Lack of professional conduct or disrespectful behavior.
b) Major Misconduct: Major misconduct, which may lead to dismissal, includes the following:
- Willful insubordination or disrespect towards superiors.
- Theft, fraud, or dishonesty involving company property or assets.
- Engaging in corrupt activities, including accepting bribes or kickbacks.
- Deliberate work slowdowns, sabotage, or inciting others to disrupt operations.
- Engaging in workplace violence, intimidation, or inappropriate behavior.
- Smoking or substance abuse on company premises.
- Disclosure of confidential company information or trade secrets.
- Involvement in illegal activities on company property, including gambling or fighting.
- Participating in or organizing strikes, protests, or unlawful assemblies.
- Sexual harassment, which includes unwelcome physical, verbal, or visual conduct of a sexual nature.
## Disciplinary Action Procedures.
## Punishment for Misconduct
The severity of punishment will correspond to the seriousness of the misconduct. Potential disciplinary actions include:
- Verbal or Written Warning: For minor misconduct or first-time offenses.
- Suspension: For up to 10 days without pay for more serious violations.
- Demotion or Salary Reduction: For repeated violations or continued performance issues.
- Termination: For major misconduct, repeated offenses, or when no improvement is seen after prior disciplinary actions.
## Procedure for Dealing with Cases of Misconduct
Birla is committed to a fair process when addressing allegations of misconduct. Employees are entitled to a clear and transparent procedure:
- Investigation Process: When misconduct is alleged, a formal inquiry will be conducted. A charge sheet will be issued to the employee outlining the specific charges. The employee will have the opportunity to submit their explanation. If the explanation is unsatisfactory, a hearing will be scheduled, during which the employee will have the right to present their case and be assisted by a colleague if desired. The inquiry will be conducted by an appointed Enquiry Officer, and the employee must attend the hearing.
- Suspension Pending Inquiry: If necessary, the employee may be suspended while the investigation is ongoing. Suspension is only effective once communicated in writing, stating the alleged offense. During the suspension period, the employee will receive a subsistence allowance based on their salary. If found guilty after the inquiry, disciplinary actions, including suspension or termination, may be enforced.
- Timing of the Inquiry: The company will ensure that disciplinary inquiries are conducted promptly and fairly. If the investigation extends beyond a reasonable time due to circumstances attributable to the employee, the subsistence allowance may be adjusted accordingly.
- Outcome of the Inquiry: Upon completion of the inquiry, if the employee is found guilty of misconduct:
- Disciplinary action will be taken, including warnings, suspension, demotion, or dismissal.
- If found not guilty, the employee will be reinstated with full pay for the suspension period.
- Appeal Process: Employees have the right to appeal disciplinary decisions. If the employee believes the action taken is unjust, they can request a review by senior management, providing any relevant evidence or clarifications.
- Confidentiality and Fair Treatment: All allegations and proceedings will be handled with the utmost confidentiality and respect for the dignity of all parties involved. Disciplinary actions will be proportionate to the severity of the misconduct and will consider the employee's previous record.
## Specific Considerations for Major Misconduct
In cases of serious offenses such as theft, dishonesty, harassment, or criminal activity, immediate action may be taken without prior warnings. These actions may include suspension pending a full investigation or immediate dismissal, depending on the nature of the misconduct.

chapters.title: Family-Friendly Programs.
chapters.text:
- The HR department, in collaboration with management, organizes family-friendly programs primarily for employees while ensuring that contracted workers are treated fairly and in accordance with statutory welfare requirements.
- Contractors operating on-site are required to comply with applicable labor welfare laws, including provisions related to working hours, leave, and statutory benefits for their workers.
- Employee Involvement: To ensure these programs are meaningful and impactful, the HR team actively engages with employee representatives or committees to gather input and feedback. This inclusive approach helps tailor initiatives that benefit all employees.
- Regular Engagement: Programs are conducted on a quarterly basis, fostering consistent participation and engagement across the workforce.
- Key Focus Areas: The programs emphasize topics that support employees in balancing personal and professional lives, such as:
- Work-life integration strategies
- Parenting and family support
- Health and wellness education
- Financial planning and literacy
- Activities and Participation: Activities include interactive parenting and work-life balance workshops, expert-led seminars, and family-focused events designed to enhance overall well-being and strengthen family engagement. Employees are encouraged to participate actively and share their suggestions for future topics and initiatives, ensuring programs remain dynamic and relevant.
- Through these programs, the organization reaffirms its commitment to fostering a supportive and inclusive work environment.
## Health and Safety of Contracted Workers
Birla is committed to ensuring a safe and healthy working environment not only for employees but also for non-employee workers, contractors, visitors, and service providers operating within company premises.
- Compliance with Legal Requirements: All contractors are required to comply with applicable occupational health and safety laws, statutory welfare provisions, and company safety standards while operating on-site.
- Induction and Safety Orientation: Non-employee and contract workers undergo mandatory safety induction training before commencing work to familiarize them with site-specific hazards, emergency procedures, and safety protocols.
- Provision of PPE: Contractors must ensure that their workers are equipped with appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). The company monitors compliance to ensure proper usage at all times.
- Risk Assessment and Hazard Control: Periodic risk assessments are conducted to identify potential hazards. Necessary control measures are implemented to prevent accidents and occupational illnesses.
- Emergency Preparedness: Contracted workers are included in fire drills, mock evacuation exercises, and emergency response training to ensure preparedness during unforeseen incidents.
- Access to Medical Facilities: Non-employee workers have access to on-site first aid facilities and emergency medical support in case of injury or illness during work hours.
- Incident Reporting Mechanism: Contractors and their workers are required to promptly report accidents, near-misses, or unsafe conditions. All incidents are investigated, and corrective actions are implemented without retaliation.
- Monitoring and Supervision: Contractor performance on health and safety parameters is regularly monitored. Non-compliance may result in corrective action, penalties, or termination of contract.
- Safe Working Hours: Working hours and rest intervals of contracted workers are reviewed to ensure compliance with legal standards and prevention of fatigue-related risks.

chapters.title: Employee Communication and Engagement
chapters.text:
## Employee Feedback and Suggestion Mechanism for Enhancing Working Conditions.
MP Birla has established a two-way communication system to ensure employees can voice concerns, suggestions, and feedback regarding working conditions. This system fosters transparency and a positive work environment.
Key features include:
Commitment: Birla is committed to fostering open and transparent communication between employees and management. These sessions aim to ensure that feedback, concerns, and suggestions from employees are heard, and responses from management are provided clearly.
Scope: This policy applies to all employees of Birla, including full-time, part-time staff, managers, and senior leadership, aiming to enhance communication and engagement throughout the company.
## Responsibility:
- The HR department is responsible for organizing and facilitating the communication sessions.
- Managers and team leaders are expected to encourage participation and engagement from their teams.
- Senior leadership, including the CEO, will actively participate and respond to employee feedback.
## Types of Two-Way Communication Sessions:
- Open Communication Channels: Employees can provide feedback via :
- Email – hr@mpbirlajute.com
- Direct communication with the supervisor or manager during team meetings or one-on-one discussions.
## Company-Wide Forums (Town Halls):
- Description: Meetings where employees from all departments meet with senior leadership to discuss company-wide updates, challenges, and concerns.
- Frequency: Held quarterly.
- Format: Presentations from senior leaders followed by a Q&A session for employees to ask questions and provide feedback.
## Departmental Feedback Sessions:
- Description: Focused meetings to address department-specific concerns, working conditions, and operational improvements.
- Frequency: Held monthly or as needed.
- Format: Informal meetings to discuss challenges and propose solutions. Feedback is shared with senior management.
## Employee-Management Dialogue Forums:
- Description: Structured forums that provide employees an opportunity to discuss workplace policies, benefits, and conditions.
- Frequency: Held bi-annually.
- Format: Employees present concerns and management responds, outlining possible actions and resolutions.
## One-on-One Feedback Sessions:
- Description: Confidential sessions for employees who prefer private settings to voice concerns or feedback.
- Frequency: Available on request.
- Format: Informal and confidential meetings between the employee and their manager or HR.
- Anonymous Reporting: Employees can raise concerns anonymously in the suggestions box near the help desk, ensuring comfort in addressing sensitive issues without fear of retaliation.
- Timely Response: Concerns are reviewed and addressed promptly, with updates provided to employees on the progress made.
- Continuous Improvement: Employee feedback is used to improve workplace policies and conditions, fostering a healthier and more collaborative work environment.
## Guidelines for Effective Communication:
- Encouraging Open Dialogue: Employees are encouraged to share thoughts, concerns, and feedback openly. Management listens attentively in a non-judgmental environment.
- Real-Time Responses: Management will respond to feedback during the session. Additional information will be followed up on if necessary.
- Anonymous Feedback Option: Employees may submit feedback anonymously through digital forms, which will be reviewed and addressed during the sessions.
- Promoting Maximum Engagement: Managers ensure that all employees are encouraged to participate and that all voices are heard.
## Session Documentation and Follow-Up:
- Meeting Minutes: HR will document key discussions, decisions, and actionable items from each session.
- Follow-Up Actions: HR will track and report back on commitments or action points, ensuring transparency and accountability.
## Encouraging Participation:
- Communication of Upcoming Sessions: HR will notify employees in advance about upcoming communication sessions, including details on topics and participation methods.
- Participation Incentives: Employees contributing meaningfully will be recognized in internal communications or invited to follow-up meetings with leadership.
## Monitoring and Evaluation:
- Employee Feedback Surveys: HR will regularly survey employees to assess the effectiveness of the sessions and identify areas for improvement.
- Annual Review: An annual review will evaluate participation rates, discussion quality, and workplace improvements.
- Continuous Improvement: Based on feedback, the format and frequency of sessions will be refined to ensure they meet employee needs effectively.

chapters.title: Technology and Information Security
chapters.text:
## Acceptable Use of IT Resources.
Birla provides IT resources, including computers, mobile devices, software, internet access, and email services, to employees for the effective performance of their job duties. The following guidelines outline the acceptable use of these resources:
- Authorized Use: IT resources are to be used solely for work-related activities, unless explicitly authorized otherwise. Personal use should be minimal and not interfere with job performance or breach any company policies.
- Security: Employees must take appropriate measures to ensure the security of IT resources, such as using strong passwords, logging out of systems when not in use, and not sharing their login credentials with others.
- Prohibited Activities: Employees are prohibited from using IT resources for any illegal or unethical activities, including:
- Accessing, storing, or transmitting material that is obscene, defamatory, or violates intellectual property rights.
- Engaging in unauthorized access to company systems, networks, or data.
- Downloading or distributing malicious software, viruses, or any other form of malware.
- Using IT resources for personal commercial gain or unauthorized political activities.
- Monitoring: All IT resources provided by Birla remain the property of the company. Birla reserves the right to monitor the usage of its IT systems to ensure compliance with these policies.
## Cybersecurity Guidelines.
Birla is committed to safeguarding its systems, networks, and sensitive data from cyber threats. Employees must adhere to the following cybersecurity guidelines to protect the company’s IT infrastructure:
- Password Security: Employees must create strong, unique passwords for all company accounts and systems. Passwords should be changed periodically and should not be shared with anyone, including colleagues.
- Phishing and Email Scams: Employees should be cautious when receiving unsolicited emails, attachments, or links. Avoid clicking on suspicious links, downloading files from unknown sources, or responding to requests for sensitive information.
- Software and Updates: Employees must ensure that all software, including antivirus programs, is kept up to date. Regular updates and patches must be installed to prevent vulnerabilities.
- Network Security: Employees are required to use a company-approved Virtual Private Network (VPN) when accessing the company network remotely. Unauthorized devices should not be connected to the company network.
- Reporting Cybersecurity Incidents: Employees must immediately report any suspected cybersecurity incidents, such as data breaches, phishing attempts, or system malfunctions, to the IT department. Swift action helps to minimize potential damage.
- Use of Personal Devices: Personal devices should be used cautiously for work-related purposes. Employees are expected to ensure their personal devices are secure and comply with Birla’s security protocols, especially when accessing corporate data remotely.
Birla is committed to protecting the privacy of its employees, customers, and stakeholders in compliance with applicable data protection laws. This policy outlines the steps employees must take to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and security of personal data.
- Collection of Personal Data: Birla collects only the necessary personal data from employees required for employment purposes, including name, contact details, and payroll information. Sensitive data, such as health-related information, is only collected with explicit consent and when legally required.
- Data Usage: Personal data should be used only for the specific purposes for which it was collected. Employees are prohibited from using personal data for unauthorized purposes, including sharing or disclosing it to third parties without consent.
- Data Storage and Security: Employees must ensure that all personal data is stored securely, either digitally or physically. Digital data should be encrypted, and physical documents should be kept in locked, secure locations.
- Data Access: Access to personal data is restricted to authorized personnel only. Employees should not access personal data unless it is required for the performance of their job duties.
- Retention and Disposal: Personal data should only be kept for as long as necessary to fulfill its purpose. Once data is no longer needed, it should be securely disposed of, whether it is in electronic or paper form.
- Employee Rights: Employees have the right to request access to their personal data, correct inaccuracies, or request that their data be deleted (subject to legal and operational requirements). Any such requests should be directed to the Human Resources department.
- Compliance: Birla complies with all applicable data protection laws and regulations. Employees are expected to follow these policies and to report any data breaches, unauthorized access, or misuse of personal data immediately to the Data Protection Officer.

chapters.title: Exit Policies
chapters.text:
## Resignation and Termination Procedures.
The procedure outlined below will be followed in cases of separation of employees from the services of the company. Separation may occur due to the following reasons:
- Resignation: An employee intending to resign must submit their resignation in writing to their immediate superior. Employees are required to serve a notice period of three months, unless otherwise stated. Employees on probation must serve a notice period of one month. The management may, at its discretion, allow payment in lieu of notice period. Any waiver of the notice period will require approval from a Director or the CEO. Employees may adjust their accrued privilege leave against the notice period if they choose. Upon acceptance of the resignation, the resignation letter should be forwarded to the HR Head for processing. Final settlement dues will be made according to company policy, with the salary for the notice period being paid in accordance with the company's guidelines.
- Termination: In case of termination, employees will be provided with sufficient reasons for the decision. For employees who have completed at least one year of continuous service, retrenchment will be carried out in accordance with the Industrial Disputes Act. Upon termination, any wages and legal dues owed will be settled before the end of the second working day.
- Separation Due to Death: In the unfortunate event of an employee’s death, the HR department will handle the complete process, including the payment of final dues to the legal heir of the deceased. This will be done after completing the necessary due diligence.
- Superannuation: Employees will retire at the age of 58 as per the company’s records. The management may grant extensions beyond this age or re-engage the employee on a contractual basis. A farewell gathering and gift will be arranged as per the company’s reward and recognition policy. Final settlement, including retirement benefits, will be processed in accordance with the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972.
## Final Settlement Process.
Upon an employee’s separation from the company, the following items must be returned to the HR department for the final settlement process:
- Company-issued PC/Laptop and all associated accessories.
- Company-provided SIM card, if applicable.
- Company-provided accommodation, furniture, and car, if applicable.
- All relevant official documents and files in the employee's possession.
The following dues will be calculated and settled at the time of separation:
- Outstanding Salary: Any unpaid salary up to the last working day.
- Leave Encashment: Encashment of earned leave, subject to eligibility and the maximum encashable limit, unless leave is adjusted against the notice period.
- Gratuity Pay: In accordance with the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972.
- Notice Pay: If the employee does not serve the required notice period or if the notice period is waived, the employee will be required to pay an amount equivalent to the basic salary for the notice period not served.
- Other Recoveries: Any other outstanding reimbursements or recoveries.
The final payment will be made via an A/c Payee cheque or credited to the employee’s bank account. The company will also issue an experience certificate at the time of release.
## Exit Interview Guidelines.
Exit interviews are an integral part of the separation process. They provide valuable feedback that helps the company improve its practices and address any concerns. Employees leaving the company are encouraged to participate in an exit interview. The following guidelines should be followed:
- The exit interview will be scheduled by the HR department and conducted in a confidential setting.
- Employees are encouraged to provide honest and constructive feedback regarding their experience with the company, including their reasons for leaving, work environment, management, and suggestions for improvement.
- All feedback received during the exit interview will be reviewed by the HR team and relevant management to identify potential areas for organizational improvement.
- The HR team will ensure that any outstanding concerns or issues raised during the exit interview are addressed in a timely and appropriate manner.
Participation in the exit interview is optional but encouraged to help improve the employee experience for future team members.

## Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy.
Bribery, corruption, and improper conduct are not tolerated at Birla. Employees must not offer, accept, or solicit bribes or any form of unethical advantage. This applies to all interactions, whether with public officials, business partners, or individuals.

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure
chapters.text:
At MP Birla Jute, we are dedicated to upholding a culture of transparency, accountability, and ethical conduct. Our whistleblower procedure provides a safe and confidential mechanism for employees, contractors, and stakeholders to report concerns related to unethical practices, fraud, corruption, or violations of company policies and applicable laws, without fear of retaliation.
## Objectives of the Whistleblower Procedure
This procedure is designed to:
- Offer a secure and confidential platform for reporting concerns.
- Protect whistleblowers from retaliation or adverse consequences.
- Facilitate timely and thorough investigation of reported issues.
## Scope
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and stakeholders associated with MP Birla Jute. It covers concerns including, but not limited to:
- Financial malpractice or fraud.
- Harassment, discrimination, or workplace misconduct.
- Bribery and Corruption
- Health and safety violations.
- Environmental breaches.
- Information security breaches.
- Violations of company policies or laws.
## Reporting a Concern
## Available Reporting Channels
Employees can report concerns through the following channels:
## Secure Email
- Concerns can be reported via email at: whistleblower@mpbirla.com
## Written Communication
- Detailed written reports can be addressed to: Whistleblower Officer, MP Birla Jute Birlapur, 24 Parganas (S), West Bengal 743 318 Kolkata, West Bengal India
## nformation to Include
When reporting, employees are encouraged to provide detailed information, including:
- Description of the issue.
- Names of individuals involved.
- Dates and locations of incidents.
- Supporting evidence, if available.
## nvestigation Process
## Acknowledgment
- All concerns will be acknowledged within 3 business days of receipt.
## Preliminary Assessment
- The Whistleblower Officer will conduct an initial review to determine if the concern requires further investigation.
## nvestigation
- A comprehensive investigation will be conducted by an independent internal team or external experts.
## Conclusion and Action
- Appropriate corrective measures will be implemented based on the findings.
- Whistleblowers will be informed of the outcome, maintaining confidentiality.
## Confidentiality and Anonymity
- All reports will be handled with the highest level of confidentiality.
- Employees may choose to remain anonymous; however, providing contact information may assist in the investigation.
## Protection Against Retaliation
- Retaliation against whistleblowers is strictly prohibited.
- Employees engaging in retaliatory actions will face disciplinary measures, up to and including termination.
## False Allegations
- Making false reports with malicious intent is a violation of company policy and will result in disciplinary action.

chapters.title: Employee Records
chapters.text:
At MP Birla Jute, we are committed to maintaining comprehensive, accurate, and up-to-date records for all employees. These records serve as a vital resource for effective workforce management, adherence to legal requirements, and fostering transparency across all employment processes.
## Purpose
The employee records management system is designed to:
- Document key details of employment history, achievements, and milestones.
- Ensure compliance with applicable labor laws and organizational policies.
- Support informed decision-making regarding employee development and management.
## Contents of Employee Records
The following categories of information are maintained as part of employee records:
- Personal Information: Full name, contact details, date of birth, emergency contacts, and current address.
- Employment History: Joining date, job title, department, responsibilities, and employment agreements.
- Compensation Details: Salary structure, bonuses, benefits, and tax information.
- Performance Records: Appraisals, promotions, disciplinary actions, awards, and feedback.
- Attendance and Leave Management: Attendance logs, leave entitlements, and patterns of absence.
- Training and Development: Certificates, professional development activities, and completed training programs.
- Exit Details: Reasons for separation, final settlement records, and resignation/termination letters.

## Confidentiality and Accessibility
- Employee records are managed with the highest level of confidentiality.
- Access is restricted to authorized personnel, and employees may submit formal requests to review their personal records.
- The company complies with all applicable laws, including those governing data protection and privacy.
## Retention and Disposal
- Records are retained for a period defined by company policy or legal requirements.
- Secure methods are used for record disposal after the retention period to prevent unauthorized access
## Documents Retention and Management
At MP Birla Jute, the systematic management of records is essential for ensuring compliance with legal regulations, achieving operational efficiency, and preserving the company’s corporate history. The Records Retention Schedule is implemented as a structured framework for managing, retaining, and securely disposing of all company documents in alignment with applicable laws and organizational needs.
Guiding Procedure:
- Categorization of Records: All records are classified into distinct categories, including employee files, financial documents, contracts, operational data, and legal records. This categorization facilitates organized management and adherence to retention requirements.
- Defined Retention Periods: Each category of records is assigned a specific retention period based on legal mandates, regulatory compliance, and business relevance.
- Access and Security: Records are securely stored in physical storage/digital storage and accessed only by authorized personnel. Confidentiality and data protection protocols are strictly enforced.
- Periodic Review: Retention schedules are periodically reviewed to reflect changes in legal requirements, regulatory updates, and operational adjustments. This ensures that records management remains relevant and compliant.
- Disposition of Records: Once the retention period has elapsed, records are disposed of securely using approved methods, such as shredding or digital data wiping, to prevent unauthorized access or misuse.
- Training and Awareness: Employees are regularly trained on records management practices, the importance of compliance with the retention policy, and secure handling of documents. A dedicated records management team monitors adherence and offers guidance on maintaining proper documentation.
